2. CC[C@@H] - This is part of the pyrrolidine ring
3. (C)N1 - Another methyl group attached to a carbon next to the nitrogen in the ring
4. Cc2ccccc2 - This is a benzyl group (CH2-phenyl) attached to the nitrogen

Let me count the different hydrogen environments:
- The two methyl groups on the ring (likely 2 different signals due to different stereochemical environments)
- The CH2 group of the benzyl substituent
- The aromatic hydrogens of the phenyl ring (typically appear as a multiplet)
- The CH groups at the stereocenters in the ring
- The remaining CH2 groups in the pyrrolidine ring

Let me count these more precisely:

1. Methyl group at first stereocenter (3H)
2. Methyl group at second stereocenter (3H)
3. Benzyl CH2 group (2H)
4. Aromatic hydrogens (5H, but may appear as fewer signals due to symmetry)
5-8. The four hydrogens in the pyrrolidine ring (likely 4 different environments due to stereochemistry)
